figures.caption: Figure 2: Distribution of sample counts with semantic loss in NSD. The histogram illustrates the semantic loss incurred when cropping original MS-COCO images to the NSD format. Semantic loss is defined as the fraction of objects in an image that lose more than 50% of their total pixels during cropping [1]. Notably, 12,901 of 73,000 images (17.7%) exhibit semantic loss.

Figure 3: Overview of the proposed neural-to-text framework. During training, a brain encoder is trained to align fMRI responses with the visual token representations extracted by a frozen VLM image encoder. In inference, the most highly activated visual tokens are selected based on brain activity and passed to the frozen VLM as semantic evidence to generate descriptive language output.
